items.title: Three Branches, One Set of Causes and Conditions — and a New Branch Opens

items.zh: 又毘鉢舍那支，最初必用善友為依。奢摩他支，尸羅圓滿之所攝受。又依善友之所攝受，於所知境真實性中有覺了欲。依尸羅圓滿之所攝受，於增上尸羅毀犯淨戒現行非法壞軌範中，若諸有智同梵行者，由見聞疑，或舉其罪，或令憶念，或令隨學；於爾所時堪忍譏論。又依所知真實覺了欲故，愛樂聽聞；依樂聞故，便發請問；依請問故，聞昔未聞甚深法義。數數聽聞無間斷故，於彼法義轉得明淨，又能除遣先所生疑。如是覺慧轉明淨故，於諸世間所有盛事，能見過患，深心厭離。如是厭心善作意故，於彼一切世間盛事不生願樂。彼由如是於諸世間增上生道無願心故，為欲斷除諸惡趣法，心生正願。又為修集能對治彼所有善法、修集一切煩惱對治所有善法，為欲證得彼對治果，亦為自心得清淨故，心生正願。如是十種能熟解脫慧成熟法，如先所說，漸次能令解脫圓滿。又隨次第已說三支。謂聞正法圓滿、涅槃為上首、能熟解脫慧之成熟。如是三支廣聖教義，謂十十種。除此更無若過若增。又此三支，當知即是修瑜伽因緣。
items.en: These three branches, it should be known, are precisely the causes and conditions for yogic cultivation.

items.zh: 何以故？由依此次第、此因、此緣，修習瑜伽方得成滿。謂依聞正法圓滿、涅槃為上首、能熟解脫慧成熟故。云何修習對治？當知略說於三位中，有十種修習瑜伽所對治法。云何三位？一、在家位，二、出家位，三、遠離閑居修瑜伽位。云何十種修習瑜伽所對治法？謂在家位中，於諸妻室，有婬欲相應貪；於餘親屬及諸財寶，有受用相應愛。如是名為處在家位所對治法。由此障礙，於一切種不能出離。
items.en: Why is this so? Because only by relying on this sequence, this cause and this condition is the cultivation of yoga brought to completion — namely complete access to hearing the true teaching, nirvāṇa held as the governing aim, and the maturing of the wisdom that ripens liberation. What is cultivating the remedies? It should be understood that, in brief, across three stages there are ten things to be remedied in the cultivation of yoga. What are the three stages? First, the stage of the householder; second, the stage of one gone forth; third, the stage of one cultivating yoga while dwelling in secluded retreat. What are the ten things to be remedied in the cultivation of yoga? In the stage of the householder there is lust, associated with sexual desire, towards one's wife; and there is craving, associated with enjoyment, towards one's other relatives and one's wealth. These are called the things to be remedied in the stage of the householder. Obstructed by these, one is in every way unable to go forth.

items.title: The Monastic's Own Affliction, and the Two Remedies That Answer Both

items.zh: 設得出家，由此尋思之所擾動為障礙故，不生喜樂。
items.en: Even having gone forth, one is disturbed and obstructed by this same rumination, and so no joy arises.

items.zh: 如是二種所對治法，隨其次第修不淨想、修無常想，當知是彼修習對治。
items.en: For these two afflictions, cultivating the contemplation of impurity and the contemplation of impermanence, in their respective order, is the remedy that must be cultivated.

items.zh: 又出家者，於出家位中，時時略有四種所作。一、常方便修善法所作。謂我於諸法常方便修為依止故，當能制伏隨愛味樂一切心識，又能如實覺了苦性。二、於無戲論涅槃信解愛樂所作。謂我當於無戲論涅槃，心無退轉，不生憂慮。謂我我今者何所在耶？三、於時時中遊行聚落乞食所作。謂我乞食受用為因，身得久住有力調適，常能方便修諸善法。四、於遠離處安住所作。謂若愛樂與諸在家及出家眾雜居住者，便有種種世間相應見聞受用諸散亂事；勿我於彼正審觀察心一境位，當作障礙。
items.en: Further, one who has gone forth has, in the stage of one gone forth, four tasks to perform from time to time, in brief. First, the task of constantly and diligently cultivating wholesome qualities: that is, 'By relying on constant, diligent cultivation of these qualities, I shall be able to subdue every state of mind that follows the relish of pleasure, and to understand the nature of suffering as it truly is.' Second, the task of conviction in and delight towards nirvāṇa, which is free of conceptual elaboration: that is, 'Towards nirvāṇa free of conceptual elaboration my mind shall not turn back, nor give rise to anxious thoughts such as: "Where, then, will my self now be?"' Third, the task of going into villages from time to time on the alms round: that is, 'With the alms food I make use of as the cause, my body will long endure, strong and well-adjusted, and I shall always be able to cultivate wholesome qualities diligently.' Fourth, the task of dwelling in a secluded place: that is, 'If I delight in living mixed together with householders and those gone forth, there will be all kinds of distracting matters bound up with worldly seeing, hearing and enjoyment; may these not become an obstacle for me at the stage of correctly and carefully contemplating with a one-pointed mind.'

items.title: Four Things a Monastic Must Always Do, and the Affliction Hidden Inside Each

items.zh: 於此四種所作事中，當知有四所對治法。於初所作，有嬾墮懈怠；於第二所作，有薩迦耶見；於第三所作，有愛味貪；於第四所作，有世間種種樂欲貪愛。
items.en: Within these four tasks, four afflictions to be remedied should be recognised. In the first, laziness and indolence; in the second, the view of a real self; in the third, craving for flavour; in the fourth, craving for the world's various pleasures.

items.zh: 如是四種所對治法，如其次第，亦有四種修習對治。一、於無常修習苦想；二、於眾苦修無我想；三、於飲食修厭逆想；四、於一切世間修不可樂想。
items.en: For these four afflictions, in their respective order, four cultivations serve as remedy: contemplating suffering within impermanence; contemplating non-self within the manifold sufferings; contemplating revulsion towards food; and contemplating the unloveliness of everything in the world.

items.zh: 又於遠離閑居方便作意位中，當知略有四種所治。何等為四？
items.en: Further, in the stage of applying attention to the practice while dwelling in secluded retreat, it should be understood that there are, in brief, four things to be remedied. What are the four?

blocks.text: The fifth branch, **cultivating the remedies**, begins: ten afflictions that obstruct yoga in three stages of life, and their remedies. Several definitions are missing from Ru-Yi's translation; the English column gives our own translation, marked as ours.

subs.head: Three branches, one set of causes

blocks.text: The second to fourth branches are "the causes and conditions for yogic cultivation". Master Cháng Bǎi: insight is the main cause; calm the most important supporting condition.
The obstacles appear in three positions: at home, after going forth, and in solitary practice.
**At home** (missing from Ru-Yi's translation): sexual craving towards one's spouse, and craving for the enjoyment of relatives and wealth. These keep one from leaving home at all.

**After going forth**: the same objects are gone, but **rumination** on them remains, so that "no joy arises", and one may even regret going forth. Venerable Miào Jìng: "I shouldn't have left; how good it would be to be with my parents." The remedies are the contemplation of **impurity** (against sexual craving) and of **impermanence** (against craving for kin and wealth). Venerable Miào Jìng: simply saying "don't think that way" does not work against beginningless habit; one needs a real method.

A renunciant has four regular tasks (defined in a passage missing from Ru-Yi's translation, 0390a10): constant practice of the good; confident delight in nirvāṇa, free of the worry "where will I be then?"; going for alms, so that the body stays strong for practice; and living in solitude, away from distracting company.

Each has its affliction and remedy: - **laziness and indolence**, countered by seeing **suffering within impermanence**. Master Cháng Bǎi: laziness is not wanting to develop good not yet arisen; indolence, not maintaining good already present; - **the view of a real self** (the fear of nirvāṇa), countered by seeing **non-self within suffering**. Venerable Miào Jìng: "Where will I be? Will there still be a me?"; - **craving for flavour**, countered by **revulsion towards food**. Master Cháng Bǎi adds a caution: someone who has lost all appetite needs the opposite, to imagine food as nectar; - **craving for worldly variety**, countered by **seeing nothing in the world as delightful**.

quiz.q: What does the treatise say these three branches are?
options: the causes and conditions for yogic cultivation
quiz.why: "These three branches, it should be known, are precisely the causes and conditions for yogic cultivation." Master Cháng Bǎi: with favourable basis plus these three, the provisions for practice are ready.

quiz.q: How do the masters divide cause and condition in yogic cultivation?
options: Cháng Bǎi: insight is the main cause, calm the most important condition; Miào Jìng: wisdom is the cause, precepts and concentration conditions
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: insight is the main cause, and calm-abiding the most important supporting condition. Venerable Miào Jìng: the wisdom of insight is the cause; the rest — precepts and concentration — are conditions, and conditions are many.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, why does joy not arise even after going forth?
options: one is disturbed and obstructed by rumination
quiz.why: "Even having gone forth, one is disturbed and obstructed by this same rumination, and so no joy arises." Master Cháng Bǎi: after going forth one no longer has the object-afflictions of sexual craving or enjoyment, but rumination remains.

quiz.q: What remedies does the treatise prescribe for these two afflictions?
options: in order, contemplation of impurity and contemplation of impermanence
quiz.why: "For these two afflictions, cultivating the contemplation of impurity and the contemplation of impermanence, in their respective order, is the remedy." Venerable Miào Jìng: whether one ordains or not, it is all impermanent — would staying home have satisfied you completely?

quiz.q: What example of ruminating thought after going forth does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: regretting ordination — "I should not have left; how good to be with my parents and loved ones"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "I shouldn't have gone forth; how good it would be to be with my parents, with my loved ones" — that is regretting ordination.

quiz.q: What four cultivations does the treatise prescribe as remedies, in order?
options: suffering within impermanence, non-self within suffering, revulsion towards food, unloveliness of the whole world
quiz.why: "Contemplating suffering within impermanence; contemplating non-self within the manifold sufferings; contemplating revulsion towards food; and contemplating the unloveliness of everything in the world."

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish laziness from indolence?
options: not wanting to develop virtues not yet arisen is laziness; not wanting to keep those already present is indolence
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: not wanting to develop virtues not yet arisen is called laziness; not wanting to keep up virtues already possessed is called indolence.
